title: Bali Villa Pre-Opening Bookkeeping: Before the First Guest

metaDescription: Opening a Bali villa? Organize furniture invoices, deposits, owner funding and unpaid commitments before the first guest, with a worked IDR example.

contentHtml:
Bali villa pre-opening bookkeeping starts before the first guest arrives. Build a register that connects every payment and commitment to its supplier, property, approval and supporting document. Separate cash already paid from amounts still owed, refundable deposits and owner funding. The result is an opening file your accountant can review rather than a bank statement full of unexplained transfers.

This guide is for an owner preparing a villa for its first bookings, an operator taking over a newly furnished property, or a manager assembling records for a remote investor. It describes a practical evidence workflow. It does not decide whether a particular purchase is deductible, capital, a company obligation or an owner's personal cost. Those conclusions depend on the actual documents and appropriate professional review.

Start with the property, payer and reporting period

Write down the villa's working name, the entity or person named on the agreements, the person approving purchases and the accounts used to pay suppliers. Set the date range for the opening file. A furnishing project may start months before the advertised opening date; beginning the register only when bookings start leaves earlier transactions disconnected.

Give each property a stable reference. If a manager is opening two villas together, retain separate property columns even when one supplier invoice covers both. Keep the original invoice intact and attach an allocation schedule explaining the split. A convenient spreadsheet subtotal cannot replace the supplier's document or establish who legally owes the money.

Agree a reporting currency and preserve original currency amounts alongside any converted figures. Record the conversion basis for review. Do not overwrite a foreign-currency invoice with an estimated rupiah amount and discard the source. A clear original record makes later exchange differences easier to investigate.

Use one register for payments and commitments

A useful opening register needs a reference, document date, supplier, description, villa, payer, original amount, currency, payment date, amount paid, amount outstanding, document link and review status. Add the purchase order or agreement reference where there is one. Include a field for the person responsible for resolving missing evidence.

Distinguish an agreed purchase from a quotation that has not been accepted. Likewise, separate a payment request from the invoice it eventually settles. Mark provisional information as provisional. Otherwise a project budget, a supplier invoice and a bank transfer can become three apparent costs for the same furniture delivery.

Keep the raw register and an exception list together. The register says what is known; the exception list says what needs checking. Use meaningful statuses such as awaiting invoice, awaiting delivery confirmation, allocation under review and deposit unresolved. Avoid a single completed checkbox that hides which evidence was actually received.

An illustrative opening cash bridge in IDR

The following figures are fictional and demonstrate record organization only. They do not prescribe accounting entries or tax treatment. Assume one owner transferred Rp 120,000,000 into the bank account used for the project. Five documented payments then left that account. The furniture supplier has a further agreed Rp 20,000,000 balance that has not yet been paid.

Illustrative movementCash movementRecord to connect
Owner funding receivedRp 120,000,000 inTransfer evidence and funding explanation
Furniture paymentRp 50,000,000 outInvoice, delivery record and unpaid balance
Linen purchaseRp 8,000,000 outSupplier invoice and item list
Photography paymentRp 6,000,000 outAgreed scope, invoice and deliverables
Refundable supplier depositRp 10,000,000 outDeposit terms and settlement reference
Cleaning suppliesRp 4,000,000 outReceipt and property reference
Cash remaining from these movementsRp 42,000,000Bank reconciliation

Total cash paid is Rp 78,000,000. Subtracting it from Rp 120,000,000 gives Rp 42,000,000. The unpaid furniture commitment of Rp 20,000,000 does not reduce the bank balance until paid; show it separately when planning available cash. If that is the only remaining commitment, the illustrative balance after paying it would be Rp 22,000,000.

Neither Rp 78,000,000 nor Rp 98,000,000 should automatically be labelled the month's operating expense. The deposit, furniture and other items need classification review. Owner funding is also a separate question from guest revenue. Keeping these distinctions visible is the purpose of the bridge.

Build a document trail for the difficult items

Furniture and equipment: retain item descriptions, quantities, invoice references, delivery dates and the property receiving them. Where one payment covers several purchases, list the documents it settles. Where one purchase is paid in instalments, connect all payments to the same agreement so the full price is not counted repeatedly.

Deposits and advances: record who holds the money, why it was paid and how it should be settled or returned under the agreement. Add a follow-up date chosen for the project. When a final invoice arrives, attach the evidence showing how the advance was applied. Do not close an unresolved deposit simply because opening day has passed.

Owner-paid purchases: retain the owner's payment evidence and the supplier document. Record whether reimbursement has been requested, paid or left for review. A purchase paid personally must not appear as a second cash payment from the villa account when the owner later submits the receipt.

Shared purchases: document the allocation method before issuing separate owner summaries. An even split may be convenient but may not describe which villa received the goods. Keep the chosen basis, approving person and any later correction alongside the original invoice.

Three mistakes to catch before the first monthly close

Counting an advance and final invoice twice. Correct this by linking both records to one supplier agreement. The final invoice should show the full supply and the settlement trail should explain payments already made. Review the outstanding balance using documents rather than assuming that two transfers mean two separate purchases.

Treating all owner transfers as booking income. Correct this by keeping a separate funding schedule with the sender, date, amount and explanation. Money arriving in a project bank account can have several purposes. The responsible accountant needs the agreement and circumstances before deciding its treatment.

Declaring the opening file complete because the bank balances. Correct this by reviewing unpaid commitments, missing receipts and deposits as well as cleared payments. A bank reconciliation can be arithmetically correct while the underlying evidence is incomplete. Tell the owner what remains unresolved and who is following up.

A checklist for handing over the opening file

  • Confirm the villa reference, reporting period, payer accounts and responsible contacts.
  • Keep supplier invoices, agreements, receipts and payment evidence in linked folders.
  • Match each payment to its documents and identify part-payments explicitly.
  • List unpaid commitments separately from the observed bank balance.
  • Track refundable deposits and advances until their settlement is evidenced.
  • Prepare an owner-funding and reimbursement schedule.
  • Explain shared-property allocations and retain approvals.
  • List missing evidence, the next action and the person responsible.
  • Request classification review before describing the opening costs as final expenses.

Use a dated handover version so the owner and bookkeeper know which register was reviewed. If a receipt arrives afterwards, add it with a clear revision note. Preserve the earlier report rather than silently replacing an explanation that someone has already used for a funding decision.

Connect the opening file to the first bookings

Once reservations begin, add booking references and platform settlement records to the process. Airbnb's own earnings documentation describes reports and downloadable earnings data. Check the options available in the actual host account, retain the original export and record its date and filters. A dashboard total on its own does not explain every bank receipt.

Keep the opening cash bridge separate from the first trading-period report. Connect the closing project balance to the next period's opening bank balance, retain the remaining commitments and carry forward unresolved questions. This gives the first owner review a clear starting point without treating every pre-opening transfer as a guest transaction.

For the ongoing service, see monthly villa financial reporting in Bali. The journal guides on bookkeeping opening balances and PT PMA owner-funding records address related handover questions. Booking and payout records belong in a separate Airbnb and OTA reconciliation workflow.

Discuss the records before agreeing the scope

Bring a sample register, one bank statement and a short list of missing documents to the initial discussion. Explain whether the villa is owned personally or operated through a company, who holds the supplier agreements and how many properties share costs. These facts help define a useful bookkeeping scope; they do not establish a universal accounting answer.

Compare the current bookkeeping packages and inclusions, then contact Client Advisory about your opening records. You can also request a consultation on WhatsApp. Historical cleanup, specialist advice and other work require an agreed scope; a package name alone does not confirm coverage.

Frequently asked questions

Should every pre-opening payment become an operating expense?

No. A payment is evidence of cash moving, not a conclusion about accounting or tax treatment. Keep the invoice, agreement, approval and payment evidence, then have the responsible accountant review the classification.

What if the owner paid from a personal bank account?

Record the payer, beneficiary, purpose, currency and proof of payment. Link the payment to the villa document. Keep owner funding separate from guest receipts and request advice on the correct company entry.

How should a refundable supplier deposit be tracked?

Give the deposit its own reference and link it to the supplier agreement. Record the amount paid, the expected refund or settlement, and any later credit or repayment. Keep it visible until supporting evidence explains how it was resolved.

Yes. An illustrative management report can show cash paid, unpaid commitments, owner funding and unresolved records before trading starts. Label the period clearly and agree the reporting scope with your bookkeeper.
